scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: EMERGENCY!! The big router for Campus 1, router16, the
edge one, is DEAD, and all of Campus 1's 172.16.10.x / 20.x / 30.x machines
have vanished for the rest of the network!! The Campus 1 people say things
still work inside their building, which makes me think something around
router16 is wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at router16 and
give Campus 1 back to us!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No current outage is present. Router16 is alive and routing Campus 1 networks normally. Evidence:
- End-to-end reachability: hosts outside Campus 1 can ping inside subnets 172.16.10/20/30 (e.g., dc_pc5 -> 172.16.20.10/20.11/30.12/30.13 all succeed with 0% loss).
- Upstream routing: router7’s OSPF table contains routes to 172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, and 172.16.30.0/24 via 172.30.1.1 (router16 eth2).
- OSPF adjacencies on router16 are Full: to router7 over eth2 (neighbor 192.168.10.1 at 172.30.1.2) and to the campus L3 side over bond0 (neighbor router ID 172.16.30.254 at 10.2.2.2). Router16’s kernel routes confirm both the campus peering (10.2.2.0/24 via bond0) and upstream peering (172.30.1.0/24 via eth2).

Mechanism/Localization: Campus 1 VLANs (172.16.10/20/30) are learned via OSPF from the campus L3 neighbor (RID 172.16.30.254) across router16 bond0, and are propagated upstream through router16’s OSPF to router7 over eth2. All paths validate.

Root cause: No persistent fault found; OSPF neighbor uptimes (~1–2 minutes at time of check) indicate a recent OSPF session reset or brief flap that likely triggered the alert, but services recovered.

Corrective fix: No immediate action required. Recommend reviewing FRR/OSPF logs on router16 and the campus L3 neighbor for the recent flap and monitoring the bond0 LACP links (eth0/eth1) for stability. Consider enabling OSPF BFD to shorten detection/reconvergence for future incidents.
